question: A waiter pins each order ticket on a rail in the kitchen and goes straight back to the tables. Why can the waiter take the next table's order right away?
options: The rail holds the ticket until a cook is free, so the waiter does not wait for the cooking
The cooks cook every dish the moment it is ordered
The ticket makes the food cook faster
The waiter only takes orders when the kitchen is empty
explanation: The rail is a queue: it holds the work until a cook (a worker) takes it, so the waiter (the producer) only spends the time it takes to pin the ticket. The cooking still takes as long as before; it just no longer holds the waiter. If tickets arrive faster than the cooks cook, the rail gets longer: a backlog.
